text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Man killed by Turkish forces on Sunday was alive before a third bullet hit him.
- The United Nations urge Turkish forces not to shoot unless their lives are in danger.
- Eleven percent of Cypriots suffer from diabetes.
- British envoy David Hannay is optimistic of a breakthrough after meeting with President Glafcos Clerides.
- A chest wound killed Petros Kakouli.
- Cyprus Airways board is lambasted for its attitude towards parliamentarians.
- Security is on the table. David Hannay has set his sights on a Clerides - (Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf) Denktash meeting.
- Members of PEO trade union working in hospitals across the island are to go on strike in protest over recent recruitments.
- Hannay launches proximity talks on the Cyprus problem focussed on security issues.
- Earth tremours are recorded in the Zygi area on the southern coast of the island, on a fault unrelated to last week's earthquake.
- Postmen warn they will impose a work-to-rule policy in protest at the government's decision to set up regional post office centres and give their administration to the private sector.
- A new meeting is expected today between the Democratic Party and the Democratic Rally over their cooperation in municipal elections in December.
